-- title

Introducing NeoDoc

Hey folks! 

I'm Alan. I'd like to introduce you to NeoDoc. 
A writing format for the Atmosphere^^1^^.


-- comment

You're seeing the raw format of this
post right now. That's because the NeoDoc
parser hasn't been integrated into the 
site yet. That's no problem. NeoDoc was
designed to make creating content easy. 
A big part of that was ensuring it's 
easy to read too.

It's like >>Markdown|
https://www.markdownguide.org/>>. 
But, you can do way more with it.

For example, when NeoDoc files are 
transformed into web pages the 
``-- comment`` sections are hidden. So, 
this note will automatically disappear 
when the parser is in place. Appropriate, 
since you'll no longer be seeing the raw 
text at that point. 


-- h2

How It Started

Three years ago, I hit my breaking point
with website tools. I was using 
Next.js^^2^^ and tried to correct a 
typo on my site. I changed a single
character and everything broke. Some
part of the process that built the site
simply stopped working. 

My site is 25 years old. I have no 
desire to deal with that shit for the 
next 25. So, I started building my own 
tools. Since I had a blank slate, I 
re-examined every aspect. That included 
using Markdown for content.


-- h2

From Scratch

One of my favorite phrases is:


-- blockquote/

Broken gets fixed. Shoddy is forever. 

-- /blockquote


As great as Markdown is for simple
blog posts, it sucks at making 
interesting pages. Anything beyond 
basic formatting and you have to roll 
your own HTML. 

For the longest time, I considered it
a shoddy experience. As I thought
about making content for the rest of 
my life, I realized it's broken. 

Or, at least, it's the wrong tool for the
job. When you can't do interesting things
in HTML without having to actually write
the HTML, it's not up to snuff. 

The realization started me down the path of 
designing a new content format. Something as 
easy to use as Markdown without sacrificing 
the power of the web's native language. 

Three years later, NeoDoc is the result.


-- h2

Where It's At

The NeoDoc parser is currently embedded in
my static site generator. Extracting it
has been on the todo list forever. It just 
wasn't a priority. Folks would have to 
make new tools to use it. Not likely, 
given the quality of the established 
website building options. 

But, you know what doesn't have established
options yet? 

**The Atmosphere**. 

It's the Wild West. Harkening back to the 
early days of the web. Before everything was 
jammed into the conformity of corporate, siloed 
social networks. 

It's awesome.


-- h2

Taking A Swing

We're at an epoch. Standards haven't been set. 
Once they have, they'll be insurmountable. 

Thanks to AT Proto, we don't have to worry 
about siloed content. We can move what
we make at our own volition. But, if we're 
not careful, we'll end up with Markdown 
again. Or, worse. We'll end up with no 
standard at all. The promise of the freedom 
of movement will be lost to a cacophony of 
content formats. Apps unintentionally locking
us in because no one else is set up process 
content the way they store it. 

And so, I'm offering NeoDoc as a path forward. 
Not just for websites, but as an interoperable 
format to underlie the Atmosphere. A human
readable way to make sure we can make the
stuff we make go where we want. 

If that sounds like the kinda thing
you're into, you can follow along
>>on this site|/>> or >>on Bluesky
|https://bsky.app/profile/neodoc.style>>.

Until next time, I'll see you in the
Atmosphere. 

->>a
|https://bsky.app/profile/alanwsmith.com>>
